subject: EdgeApps: TTFT & Concurrency acceptance checklist and validation plan
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@edgeapps.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeApps: TTFT & Concurrency acceptance checklist and validation plan

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As discussed, I attached a concise acceptance checklist for the performance bar in the MAP plus a reproducibility plan so your infra team can run the same workload. High level: we want parity on TTFT (time-to-first-token), stable p95 latency under your target concurrency, and no more than a 10% throughput delta compared to our reference runs at similar instance types.

Key asks for EdgeApps before we sign off:
- Run the repro script (repro-instructions.sh) on a single M60-equivalent instance and send back the ttft_concurrency_results_run3.csv.
- Confirm load generator (wrk vs. internal harness) and the exact batching / KV-cache settings used. Differences here are the most common source of delta.
- If you plan to use quantized weights, please note that our reference runs used q4_0; call that out.

I've included an abbreviated timeline in the MAP: 48h for customer repro, 24-48h for Redwood triage, then final sign-off. If you want a canary rollout instead of a full cutover, we can add that step.

Attachments: EdgeApps_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP lanes + acceptance criteria), repro-instructions.sh, redwood-run-log-run3.txt

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Also, Stan from Benchmark Labs will help with a quick independent validation; he prefers wrk-style steady-state runs.

I'll upload results to the Drive link by EOD Wednesday.

On Mon, Jun 21, 2026 at 11:03 AM Alice Chen <alice@edgeapps.com> wrote:
> Thanks Aditya — this is great. We're going to kick off the repro today. Quick clarification: our infra team currently runs a custom load harness that keeps persistent connections and warms the model for 30s before measuring. Your repro script looks like a cold-start per-request test. Which one should we run to match your baseline?

Great question — sorry for the ambiguity. We actually need two runs to fully align:
1) Warmed steady-state (30s warm, measure next 60s) using your harness or wrk; this is the primary throughput/latency comparison for steady-state SLAs.
2) Cold-start TTFT profile: single-request cold-starts spaced 10s apart to capture first-token variance.

The attached repro-instructions.sh includes both modes (flags --warm and --cold). Notes:
- Use the model variant tag redwood/v2.3.1-q4_0 to match our reference.
- Set batch_window_ms to 5 for steady-state. If your harness disables batching, please record that.
- Record p50/p95/p99 and per-request TTFT.

If you want us to run a reference job in your account (we can request temporary access), we can also produce a run on identical instance types and share the logs. Monica, Vivek — can you confirm we're ok to request temporary access for a one-off repro in EdgeApps' staging project?

Thanks,
Aditya
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@edgeapps.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeApps: TTFT & Concurrency acceptance checklist and validation plan

Hi Alice —

We're fine requesting temporary access for a one-off run; Vivek and I will coordinate IAM scope (read-only + run jobs) and keep it limited to the staging project. That approach usually removes a lot of tooling-variance noise.

Also a heads-up on a common discrepancy we saw last quarter: some customers run tokenizers at the client and send pre-tokenized inputs, which reduces measured TTFT on our side. Please confirm whether EdgeApps will send raw text or pre-tokenized payloads.

We'll plan to triage any >15% p95 delta in the following ways:
- Check batching/batch_window_ms differences
- Verify KV-cache warm behavior and eviction policy
- Compare tokenization (client vs server)
- Re-run with Redwood-run harness (we provide a container) to remove harness differences

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Stan Iverson <stan@benchmarklabs.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice@edgeapps.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeApps: TTFT & Concurrency acceptance checklist and validation plan

Quick note from the independent validator: we completed a preliminary steady-state run using wrk with persistent connections. At EdgeApps' target concurrency (64 virtual users) we saw p95 latency ~1.35x higher than Redwood's reference runs, but TTFT on cold-starts was aligned within 5%. We also captured the raw logs and attached a p95 breakdown (ttft_concurrency_results_run3.csv).

Initial hypothesis: the difference looks like it stems from different batch_window_ms (our run implicitly batched at 20ms due to client batching). Suggestion: re-run with batch_window_ms=5 on EdgeApps harness or run Redwood container in your staging project so we can eliminate harness variance.

Happy to sync for 30m tomorrow to go through logs.

—Stan

support@benchmarklabs.io
